newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: European security summit ends, row put aside.
newsitem.headline: European security summit ends, row put aside.

text.p: A European summit ended on Tuesday with a pledge that all countries would have security and peace in the 21st century, after a row between Armenia and Azerbaijan was put to one side.

The row, over the disputed enclave of Nagorno-Karabakh, had threatened to block the summit communique because all 54 members of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) had to agree on it.

Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres declared the two-day summit closed just after 1400 GMT, urging all nations present to live up to their commitments on human rights, democracy and security issues.
"We owe it to our people, who gave us their trust, we owe it to future generations and we owe it to history," he said.

Earlier, Armenia and Azerbaijan agreed to remove part of the summit declaration which referred to the long-running problem over Nagorno-Karabakh. The two countries went to war over the region in 1988 but have since agreed a ceasefire.
The debate in Lisbon underlined how difficult ethnic problems and regional conflicts are to solve now that the old East-West divide of the Cold War has gone.
